session_covered: US session of Monday 19 October (late-session figures; Wall Street had not yet closed)
intro: Covers the US session of Monday 19 October. The brief was compiled about 25 minutes before the New York close, so US figures are late-session prints and may move slightly by the bell; European figures were not separately sourced.
footnotes: US index and VIX figures are late-session prints (about 15:35 New York time) from Yahoo Finance, consistent with Trading Economics; final closes may differ slightly.
Yield: Yahoo Finance 5.14% (+4 bp from 5.10%); Trading Economics shows about 5.15%.

Brent: Trading Economics CFD price (US$109.29, -0.52%) shown, consistent with the previous brief's series; other providers quote lower levels (roughly US$106-108) because of contract and timing differences, but also show a small decline.
Gold, AUD/USD and iron ore are CFD-based reference prices from a single source (Trading Economics).

setup.summary: SPI 200 futures are around 8,791 (December contract), down roughly 0.35-0.55% on the day session's settlement (Investing.com -0.35%, TradingView -0.55%; the midpoint of -0.45% is used). Applied to Monday's ASX 200 cash close of 8,845.70 (+0.44%, a five-week high), that implies an open near 8,806, about 40 points or 0.45% lower (range roughly 31-49 points). The soft futures reading sits oddly against a higher S&P 500 and Nasdaq, but both sources agree on direction; higher US yields and oil, and a flat Dow, are consistent with a cautious lead for the broader market.

local_events: No major scheduled Australian data release confirmed.
RBA Deputy Governor Hauser speaks on Wednesday 21 October.
Company results and updates: not confirmed (FNArena's calendar is paywalled).
what_moved: A rebound in AI and chip stocks drove the US session after the sector's worst week since June: the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose about 2% after an eight-day slide of roughly 15.7%, lifting the Nasdaq Composite 1.4% and the S&P 500 0.6%, while the Dow was essentially flat as most stocks outside tech were soft. The VIX fell about 9% to just above 18. Crude rose again, with US oil up about 2% near US$104/bbl on Houthi attacks and renewed strikes on Saudi energy facilities, and the 10-year Treasury yield edged up to about 5.14%. S&P 500 sector performance was not available.

news.headline: AI and chip stocks rebound after worst week since June
news.summary: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose about 2% after an eight-day slide, with Amazon up 4.8% on a broker top-pick call and Intel up nearly 3% on an upgrade. CoreWeave slipped on concerns over its roughly US$50 billion debt load despite an analyst upgrade.

news.headline: Oil climbs on Middle East supply risks
news.summary: US crude reversed earlier losses to rise about 2.3% to nearly US$104 a barrel after Houthi attacks in Yemen and renewed strikes on Saudi energy, airport and military facilities. Brent remains above US$100.

news.headline: Fed offers no guidance; rate-hike odds for October are low
news.summary: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh gave no guidance on the 27-28 October meeting, and market odds of an October hike fell to roughly 15%. The 10-year Treasury yield sits near 5.1%.

news.headline: ASX 200 closes at five-week high
news.summary: The ASX 200 rose 0.44% to 8,845.70 on energy, mining and bank gains, helped by a China third-quarter GDP beat. RBA Assistant Governor Kent questioned whether rates are restrictive enough after September's hike.

news.headline: Big-tech earnings next in focus
news.summary: SpaceX reports Tuesday and Meta and Tesla report Wednesday, with investors watching how the AI build-out is financed after last week's selloff.

news.headline: Australian CPI and RBA decision loom
news.summary: Economists point to the September-quarter CPI on 28 October as the key input to the RBA's rate decision on 3 November.

coming_up: Wednesday 21 October: RBA Deputy Governor Hauser speaks, and Meta and Tesla report in the US. The Fed meets 27-28 October, Australian Q3 CPI is due 28 October, and the RBA decides on 3 November.
